name: STM32WLE5CCU6
title: Sub-GHz wireless Arm Cortex-M4 microcontroller, 150 MHz to 960 MHz (G)FSK, (G)MSK and BPSK radio (LoRa on STM32WLE5), up to 256 KB flash, 64 KB SRAM
summary: A single-chip long-range radio and Cortex-M4 MCU at up to 48 MHz, with 64 to 256 KB of flash and 20 to 64 KB of SRAM. The sub-GHz transceiver covers 150 MHz to 960 MHz with (G)FSK in both directions and (G)MSK and BPSK in transmit; the STM32WLE5 parts add LoRa, which the STM32WLE4 parts, this one among them, do not have. It has a +15 dBm low-power PA and a +22 dBm high-power PA, an on-chip SMPS, a 12-bit ADC, a 12-bit DAC, two comparators, AES, PKA and a true RNG, and runs from 1.8 V to 3.6 V down to 31 nA in Shutdown. Packages are a 7 x 7 mm UFQFPN48 and a 5 x 5 mm UFBGA73.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M4 with MPU and DSP instructions, 48 MHz, 1.25 DMIPS/MHz
128 KB flash, 48 KB SRAM (16 KB SRAM1 + 32 KB SRAM2)
150 MHz to 960 MHz; (G)FSK RX/TX, (G)MSK and BPSK TX; no LoRa on STM32WLE4
up to +15 dBm (RFO_LP), up to +22 dBm (RFO_HP)
VDD 1.8 V to 3.6 V; VBAT 1.55 V to 3.6 V
Shutdown 31 nA, Standby 360 nA, Stop 2 with RTC 1 µA, at VDD = 3 V
RX 4.47 mA FSK 4.8 Kbit/s (SMPS); TX 23.5 mA at +14 dBm, 120 mA at +22 dBm (868 to 915 MHz, 3.3 V)
UFBGA73, 5 x 5 mm, 0.5 mm pitch, 43 GPIOs

operation.text: The sub-GHz radio is a subsystem beside the Cortex-M4 MCU. The CPU runs the radio's low-layer stack together with the application and talks to the radio over an internal SPI (SUBGHZSPI); the radio reports events by interrupts and shows a BUSY state while it cannot accept commands.

The Cortex-M4 carries DSP instructions and an MPU with up to eight regions, each split into eight subregions, sized from 32 bytes to the full 4 GB; the MPU can be left unused. The ART accelerator, an instruction prefetch queue and branch cache in front of the 64-bit-wide flash, gives the equivalent of zero-wait-state execution from flash up to 48 MHz on CoreMark.

One bank of up to 256 KB in 2 KB pages, read and written 72 bits at a time (64 data bits plus 8 ECC bits), with page and mass erase. ECC corrects single-bit errors and detects double-bit errors; the failing address is in FLASH_ECCR. Option bytes set readout protection (RDP Level 0 none; Level 1 blocks flash access while debug, SRAM boot or the bootloader is in use; Level 2 also disables debug, SRAM boot and the bootloader for good), write protection of two areas in 4 KB steps, and two execute-only PCROP areas in 2 KB steps, with PCROP_RDP choosing whether a PCROP area is erased on a Level 1 to Level 0 change.

Up to 64 KB in two blocks: SRAM1 up to 32 KB at 0x2000 0000 and SRAM2 up to 32 KB at 0x2000 8000, directly after SRAM1 and mirrored at 0x1000 0000. SRAM2 has hardware parity and can be kept in Standby. Both run at zero wait states at every CPU clock.

AES with 128- and 256-bit keys in ECB, CBC, CTR, GCM, GMAC and CCM modes, served by DMA on two channels; a PKA for RSA, Diffie-Hellman and ECC over GF(p) in the Montgomery domain (modular exponentiation to 3136 bits, ECDSA sign and verify to 521 bits); a true RNG giving 32-bit samples from an analog entropy source; a CRC unit for 8-, 16- and 32-bit words. Each device carries a 64-bit UID and a 96-bit die ID.

The BOOT0 pin and the BOOT1 option bit pick boot from main flash, from system memory (the bootloader, which loads code over USART or SPI) or from SRAM. If BOOT0 selects main flash but the first flash word is empty, the device boots the bootloader instead, which reconfigures some GPIOs (AN2606). Setting nSWBOOT0 = 0 and nBOOT0 = 1 in the option bytes forces boot from main flash regardless of BOOT0.

LoRa (STM32WLE5 only): bandwidth 7.8 kHz to 500 kHz, spreading factor 5 to 12, 0.013 to 17.4 Kbit/s. FSK and GFSK in RX and TX: 0.6 to 300 Kbit/s. (G)MSK in TX: 0.1 to 10 Kbit/s. BPSK in TX only, at 100 and 600 bit/s. The radio meets LoRaWAN v1.0 and ETSI EN 300 220, EN 300 113, EN 301 166, FCC CFR 47 parts 15, 24, 90 and 101 and ARIB STD-T30, T-67 and T-108.

The modem output modulates the RF-PLL directly, with optional pre-filtering of the bit stream to lower adjacent-channel power, and the PLL drives one of two PAs. The high-power PA on RFO_HP gives up to +22 dBm and needs its regulator (REG PA) fed from VDD through VDDPA; its highest output falls with the supply, +22 dBm at 3.3 V down to +16 dBm at 1.8 V. The low-power PA on RFO_LP gives up to +15 dBm over the whole 1.8 V to 3.6 V range with REG PA fed from the 1.55 V VFBSMPS rail. Both PAs are programmable in 32 steps of about 1 dB, with programmable ramp timing for regulatory masks.

A differential LNA feeds a quadrature mixer to a low IF, then low-pass filters and a sigma-delta ADC into the digital modem, which decimates, mixes down, filters the channel and demodulates. The local oscillator sits below the wanted signal (frf = flo + fif). The I/Q imbalance is calibrated automatically at start-up, and again on command, to raise image rejection. Most settings use a low IF; the IF for each bandwidth setting is in the intermediate frequency tables, and LORA_BW_500 runs at zero IF.

The RF-PLL synthesizes the local oscillator for both TX and RX over the continuous 150 MHz to 960 MHz range, with automatic calibration, from the 32 MHz HSE32 reference. HSE32 runs from a 32 MHz crystal (specified for the NX2016SA and NX1612SA) on OSC_IN/OSC_OUT with on-chip trimming capacitors and no external load capacitors, or from a clipped-sine TCXO coupled into OSC_IN through 220 Ω and a series capacitor; PB0-VDD_TCXO can supply the TCXO from an internal regulator at 1.6 V to 3.3 V, 4 mA max.

VDD (1.8 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/Os, reset, power management, internal clocks and the low-power regulator. VDDSMPS and VDDRF (1.8 V to 3.6 V) are wired to the same supply as VDD so that all three follow one sequence. VFBSMPS (1.45 V to 1.62 V, 1.55 V typ) feeds the main regulator and comes from the SMPS output; VDDRF1V55 is connected to it on the board. VDDA (0 V to 3.6 V) feeds the ADC, DAC, VREFBUF and comparators and is independent of VDD; it needs 1.62 V for the ADC and comparators, 1.71 V for the DAC without buffer, 1.8 V with buffer and 2.4 V for VREFBUF, and goes to VDD when none of them is used. VBAT (1.55 V to 3.6 V) keeps the RTC, tamper logic, LSE and backup registers when VDD is absent.

VREF+ is the ADC and DAC reference, or the VREFBUF output. With VDDA below 2 V it equals VDDA; with VDDA at 2 V or more it lies between 2 V and VDDA. It may be grounded while the ADC and DAC are off. VREFBUF gives about 2.048 V (VRS = 0, VDDA ≥ 2.4 V) or 2.5 V (VRS = 1, VDDA ≥ 2.8 V); with VREFBUF off an external reference can drive VREF+. In the UFQFPN48 VREF+ is joined to VDDA inside the package.

While VDD is below 1 V the other supplies (VDDA) stay below VDD + 300 mV; above 1 V they are independent. During power-down VDD may briefly drop below the others only if the energy fed into the device stays under 1 mJ, which lets decoupling capacitors discharge at different rates.

Two regulators run in parallel: an LDO and a step-down SMPS. After POR or an NRST reset the LDO is selected; software turns the SMPS on (SMPSEN in PWR_CR5, or the radio's SetRegulatorMode command) and the SMPS choice wins over the LDO; SMPSRDY in PWR_SR2 shows the mode in use. While the radio is in Standby with HSE32 or active, the mode does not change until the radio goes back to Standby or Sleep. In Stop 1, Stop 2 and Standby with the radio idle both are off, and on wakeup the SMPS returns to the SMPSEN setting, which Stop and Standby retain. SUBGHZ_SMPSC2R sets the SMPS maximum load current and SUBGHZ_PCR the LDO and SMPS inrush. The SMPS depends on its clock and can be destroyed if the clock stops, so its clock detector (SUBGHZ_SMPSC0R.CLKDE, off by default) is turned on before the SMPS: on a clock failure it shuts the SMPS and falls back to the LDO. Without the SMPS, the inductor between VLXSMPS and VFBSMPS can be left off the board.

POR/PDR with brownout reset: BOR0 is always on (except in Shutdown); four higher BOR levels are selected by option byte and then work in every mode but Shutdown, holding the device in reset until VDD passes the chosen threshold and resetting it when VDD falls below. A PVD compares VDD with one of seven thresholds and interrupts on crossing either way; with its lowest threshold and EWPVD set in PWR_CR3 it watches the supply needed by the radio, and only a drop below the level wakes the device. PVM3 checks VDDA against a fixed threshold. A radio end-of-life monitor flags VDD too low for the radio, at which point software stops radio activity.

The main regulator output (VCORE) has two ranges: range 1 allows SYSCLK up to 48 MHz with the fastest flash reads; range 2 allows up to 16 MHz with slower flash reads; flash write and erase work in both. The main regulator is fed from VDD during power-on and on wakeup from Stop 1, Stop 2, Standby or Shutdown, and from the LDO/SMPS afterwards. The low-power regulator supplies VCORE in the low-power modes.

The VBAT domain (RTC, LSE, backup registers and three tamper pins) runs from VBAT when VDD is absent, switching over automatically; VBAT can be a battery, a supercapacitor, or VDD. An internal charger can charge VBAT through 5 kΩ or 1.5 kΩ (VBRS) while VDD is present. In VBAT operation, external interrupts and RTC events do not bring the device out of it.

After reset the device runs in Run, range 1. Sleep stops the CPU clock with peripherals running. LPRun runs below 2 MHz on the low-power regulator, and LPSleep is entered from LPRun. Stop 0 and Stop 1 keep SRAM1, SRAM2 and all registers and stop the VCORE clocks (PLL, MSI, HSI16 and HSE32 off; LSI and LSE may run); Stop 0 keeps the main regulator on for the fastest wakeup at a higher current, Stop 1 uses the low-power regulator. Stop 2 powers off part of VCORE and keeps SRAM1, SRAM2, the CPU and some peripherals. The clock on leaving Stop is MSI up to 48 MHz or HSI16. Standby powers off VCORE, optionally keeping SRAM2 on the low-power regulator (RRS in PWR_CR3); the RTC, radio and PVD may stay on and the PVD uses its lowest level. Shutdown also stops LSI, keeps only LSE and the RTC, and does not monitor the supply. Standby and Shutdown exit on MSI at 4 MHz. The radio can stay active on its own in Stop and Standby; in Shutdown it is forced to Deep-sleep.

Under and after reset the I/Os are in analog mode with the Schmitt trigger off, to save current, except the five JTAG/SWD pins, which have pull-up or pull-down. The internal reset pull-up is turned off when the reset comes from inside.

SYSCLK comes from HSI16 (16 MHz RC, ±1 % factory trimmed), MSI (100 kHz to 48 MHz, 4 MHz after reset), HSE32 or the PLL. LSI (32 kHz RC) clocks the IWDG and optionally the RTC; LSE (32.768 kHz crystal) clocks the RTC and can lock MSI. AHB, APB1 and APB2 all reach 48 MHz. Peripheral kernel clocks are selectable: ADC from SYSCLK, HSI16 or PLLP; (LP)U(S)ARTs from SYSCLK, HSI16, LSE or PCLK, waking from Stop only on HSI16 or LSE; I2C from SYSCLK, HSI16 or PCLK, waking from Stop only on HSI16; I2S2 from HSI16, PLLQ or I2S_CKIN; LPTIMs from LSI, LSE, HSI16, PCLK or LPTIMx_IN1, working in Stop only on LSI, LSE or the external input; RTC from LSE, LSI or HSE32/32; RNG from PLLQ, MSI, LSI or LSE; the DAC uses LSI in sample-and-hold. SysTick runs from HCLK1/8 or HCLK1. MCO and LSCO bring clocks out.

Each GPIO is an input (floating, pull-up or pull-down), a push-pull or open-drain output, or an alternate function, most sharing digital or analog functions; the GPIOs sit on AHB for fast toggling, and the alternate-function setup can be locked. They sink or source up to ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH, within the package totals. Most are 5 V tolerant (FT); PB0 is 3 V tolerant (TT). An input held at an intermediate level draws Schmitt-trigger current, so unused or floating pins are set to analog or driven to a fixed level.

Two DMA controllers with seven channels each; DMAMUX1 maps any DMA-capable peripheral to any of the 14 channels, with four software priorities, byte/half-word/word transfers with packing, circular buffers and up to 65536 items. The NVIC handles up to 62 maskable interrupt channels and 16 priority levels; the EXTI routes wakeup events and interrupts from configurable and direct lines.

One 12-bit SAR ADC, up to 2.5 Msps, with up to 12 external channels and internal channels for the temperature sensor (VIN[12]), VREFINT (VIN[13]), VBAT/3 (VIN[14]) and the DAC output. Single or scan conversions, a hardware oversampler of up to 256 samples reaching 16 bits, an analog watchdog, timer triggers, DMA, and auto power-down between conversions; its clock is independent of the CPU clock. A calibration after each power-up is advised. Below VDDA = 2.4 V the analog switch booster (BOOSTEN) is turned on, and turned off above.

The sensor's output rises linearly with temperature and is factory calibrated: TS_CAL1 holds the ADC result at 30 °C and TS_CAL2 at 130 °C, both at VDDA = VREF+ = 3.3 V. Without calibration it suits only relative readings. VREFINT, a bandgap, feeds the ADC and comparators; its value at 30 °C and 3.3 V is stored as VREFINT_CAL.

One 12-bit channel (8- or 12-bit modes) from a resistor string with an output buffer that can be bypassed (BOFFx), factory and user offset trimming, noise and triangle wave generation, DMA, and triggers from timers or external events. A low-power sample-and-hold mode holds the output on an internal or external capacitor, refreshed from LSI.

Two rail-to-rail comparators with programmable speed, hysteresis and output polarity; the minus input can be an I/O or VREFINT or its 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4. They wake the device from Stop, interrupt, give timer breaks, and can pair as a window comparator.

TIM1 is a 16-bit advanced timer with four channels, three complementary outputs with dead time, and break inputs. TIM2 is a 32-bit four-channel timer with encoder support. TIM16 and TIM17 are 16-bit with one channel and one complementary output. LPTIM1, LPTIM2 and LPTIM3 are 16-bit low-power timers that keep running in Stop on LSE, LSI or an external clock and can wake the device; LPTIM1 works down to Stop 2 and has encoder mode, LPTIM2 and LPTIM3 to Stop 1. The IWDG (12-bit, LSI clocked) works in Stop and Standby; the WWDG is a 7-bit window watchdog with an early-warning interrupt. SysTick is a 24-bit down-counter.

A BCD calendar RTC with alarms and a 32-bit sub-second wakeup counter that keeps running through every mode and reset while its supply holds, including VBAT mode. Twenty 32-bit backup registers are kept in all low-power modes and VBAT mode and are protected by tamper detection: three tamper pins (edge or level, with or without filter) and four internal tamper sources.

Three I2C (Sm, Fm, Fm+ with 20 mA drive, SMBus and PMBus, wakeup on address match; I2C3 down to Stop 2). The SDA/SCL pins are not true open drain: the PMOS to VDD is disabled but present. Two USARTs up to 4 Mbit/s with LIN, IrDA, smartcard (ISO 7816), SPI master, RS485 driver enable and wakeup from Stop at up to 200 kbaud. One LPUART that wakes from Stop at up to 220 kbaud and runs to 9600 baud on LSE alone. Two SPIs to 16 Mbit/s (SPI2S2 also I2S, with Philips, MSB/LSB-justified and PCM standards).

A serial-wire/JTAG debug port: SWD uses two pins (SWDIO on JTMS, SWCLK on JTCK) and a sequence on TMS switches between JTAG-DP and SW-DP; the other JTAG pins can then be GPIOs. The RF debug signals (RF_BUSY, RF_IRQx, DEBUG_SUBGHZSPI_x) can be brought out on GPIOs.

Each supply pair is decoupled with ceramic capacitors placed as close as possible to, or under, its pins on the PCB underside: 100 nF per VDD pin plus one 4.7 µF; VDDA 10 nF plus 1 µF; VREF+ 100 nF plus 1 µF; VDDSMPS 4.7 µF; VFBSMPS/VDDRF1V55 470 nF after a 15 µH SMPS inductor from VLXSMPS. The 100 nF capacitors are good-quality ceramic. The UFQFPN48 exposed pad is soldered to ground.

The 32.768 kHz crystal and its load capacitors sit as close as possible to the OSC32_IN/OSC32_OUT pins. No resistor is fitted across the crystal; adding one is not allowed. LSEDRV sets one of four drive levels. In bypass mode the oscillator is off and OSC32_IN takes an external clock as a normal GPIO input.

NRST has a permanent internal pull-up (RPU). A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, close to the device, guards against parasitic resets; whatever drives the pin pulls it below VIL(NRST) max, or the reset is ignored.

The source resistance RAIN is kept within the maximum for the chosen sampling time and resolution (maximum RAIN table). PCB plus pad capacitance on the input lowers accuracy; a lower fADC compensates for a large one.

RF figures such as sensitivity and TX current are given up to 85 °C. The radiated RF power (below 4 mW) need not be taken out of the dissipation, and with the SMPS on part of the loss goes into the inductor, mainly through its ESR.
